item.title: Fermions fields inside the geometric algebra of spacetime
item.description: arXiv:2611.12939v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The (signed) basis versors of the geometric algebra of space-time form the extraspecial groups of order 32. Ignoring signs and the unit element, we show that the remaining fifteen normalized basis versors can be written as, or factorized into, a unit space bivector (of three-dimensional space) and an isoversor. Isoversors are: the volume trivector of space, the pseudoscalar, and the basis time-axis vector. Our first result is that this central product structure, already known for extraspecial groups, also holds in the geometric algebra of space-time and is crucial for exhibiting generators of continuous groups in the algebra. In a second main result, inspired by Hestenes' 1982 paper ``Space-time structure of weak and electromagnetic interactions'', we uncover two pairs of special unitary groups of order two and three (in various representations). A rich algebraic structure emerges, leading us to our third main result: the description inside the geometric algebra of space-time of thirty-two flavorless particles of matter and antimatter. The sixteen matter particles, four leptons (left/right with up/down isospins) and four triplets of quarks (with three colors in addition to chirality and isospin), are gathered four by four into quadrispinors in two different ways: particles in a quadrispinor have either the same color or the same isospin and chirality. Thanks to this twofold distribution of the sixteen matter particles inside four quadrispinors, the same continuous group based on the isoversors produces the electroweak and strong gauge symmetry. However, chirality forbids the gauge mixing of left and right particles, which motivates the restriction to SU(2) $\times$ U(1) for the electroweak interaction. Finally, as a fourth main result, we thoroughly study the dynamics of quadrispinors by generalizing the conventional treatment of bispinors in geometric algebra.
item.dc:creator: Gatien Verley

item.title: Dust matter cosmology in modified symmetric teleparallel $f(Q,T)$ gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.12986v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the nonlinear $f(Q,T)$ gravity model, $f(Q,T) = \alpha Q^n + \beta T + \gamma$, which represents a nontrivial coupling between geometry and matter in the context of a dust-dominated Universe. The model parameters $(H_0, \alpha, \beta, \gamma, n)$ are constrained using recent cosmological observations, including Hubble parameter measurements $H(z)$, the Pantheon+SH0ES dataset, and DESI BAO data. The analysis shows that the Hubble constant exhibits dataset-dependent variations, reflecting the persisting Hubble tension, while $\alpha$ and $\gamma$ are tightly constrained and $\beta$ remains weakly determined. The nonlinear exponent $n$ introduces an additional degree of freedom that enhances the model's flexibility in reproducing observational trends. The cosmographic diagnostics, including the deceleration, jerk, snap, and lerk parameters, indicate a Universe transitioning from early deceleration to late-time acceleration, with present values closely aligned with $\Lambda$CDM predictions and far-future behavior approaching a de Sitter phase. These results demonstrate that the nonlinear $f(Q,T)$ model provides a simple and viable framework to describe late-time cosmic acceleration, accommodate observational tensions, and reproduce $\Lambda$CDM-like dynamics with subtle deviations.
item.dc:creator: M. Koussour, A. Altaibayeva, G. Bekova, A. \c{C}al{\i}\c{s}kan, E. G\"udekli, S. Muminov, J. Rayimbaev

item.title: Entropy: the Route from the Gaussian Field to the Statistical Mechanics of the Thermal Radiation
item.description: arXiv:2611.13054v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Maximum Entropy or canonical typicality applied to the electromagnetic field can provide starting points for arriving at the Bose distribution of the photon numbers of thermal radiation, but they rely on statistical postulates whose experimental testability is controversial. Here we start from experimentally verifiable assumption of Gaussianity of the electromagnetic field. We analyze the field by projecting it onto orthonormal time-frequency basis functions with unitary bandwidth duration product that represent field's orthogonal time-frequency modes. Through the Glauber-Surashdan representation, we see that the joint density operator of the modes in the photon number basis factorize into diagonal density operators with geometric coefficients of individual modes, while the mean photon occupations of the modes remains still unknown. The independent imposition of Clausius' relation on each one of the entropies and energies of the modes leads to Bose's mean photon occupancy. Thus, our main claim is that for the first time Bose statistics is recovered in the paper under explicit, experimentally verifiable statistical assumptions, without assuming any statistical postulate that is not directly experimentally verifiable. From the mean occupation numbers, the Boltzmann distribution of the energy of matter particles of the material that generates/absorbes the radiation is then derived by retracing in the backward direction the Einstein-Feynman detailed balance.
item.dc:creator: Arnaldo Spalvieri

item.title: Does quantum mechanics apply to macroscopic objects? How to define macro?
item.description: arXiv:2410.17298v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: According to Quantum Mechanics a narrow wave-packet of the center of mass of any macroscopic object should smear out after some time. The problem is usually waved out by assuming that due to their heavy masses this occurs over astronomical times. Without a clear definition of macroscopic objects this remains ambiguous. On the other hand, Quantum Mechanics allows and energetically even prefers largely smeared out c.m. states that never been seen. Why is this the real state of the world we know? Does it suggest a micro-macro threshold with different theoretical descriptions? Does offer micro-miniaturization a hope for answering these questions?
item.dc:creator: Ladislaus Alexander B\'anyai

item.title: Equivalence between the pair correlation functions of primes and the four-point correlation functions of spins in a two-dimensional Ising model with randomly distributed competing interactions
item.description: arXiv:2508.14938v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we prove the equivalence between the pair correlation functions of primes, and the four-point correlation function of spins in a two-dimensional (2D) Ising model with a mixture of ferromagnetic and randomly distributed competing interactions. At first, we prove that the four-point connected correlation function of spins in the competing 2D Ising model is larger than zero in the temperature range from zero to infinite, because of nonlinear terms of spin operators. Second, we prove that the four-point connected correlation function of spins is equivalent to the pair correlation function of energy levels in the competing 2D Ising model. Third, we prove that the pair correlation function of the energy levels of the competing 2D Ising model is equivalent to the pair correlation function of nontrivial zeros of the Dirichlet function (including the Riemann zeta function). Fourth, we prove that the pair correlation function between the nontrivial zeros of the Dirichlet function is equivalent to the pair correlation function of primes p_n and p_(n + Delta n) = p_n + q with Delta n = 1,2, ... for every even q. In a conclusion, we have proven that the pair correlation function of the primes p_n and p_(n + Delta n) = p_n + q for every even q is larger than zero.
item.dc:creator: Zhidong Zhang

item.title: Signs of Possible High-Temperature Superconductivity in Graphite Intercalated with Lithium-Based Alloys
item.description: arXiv:2510.03256v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We report experimental results indicating possible high-temperature superconductivity in graphite intercalation compounds synthesized with lithium-based alloys. Temperature-dependent measurements of magnetic moment, trapped magnetic flux, and electrical resistance reveal transitions with critical temperatures (Tc) in the range of 240-350 K at ambient pressure, depending on the intercalation metals and synthesis conditions. The highest Tc values and largest high-Tc volume fractions (< 0.1 %) were observed in graphite samples intercalated with ternary Sr-Ca-Li alloy. Our results and analyses suggest that the observed transitions originate from local superconductivity rather than intrinsic magnetic properties of the intercalated graphite, which may be an alternative explanation. Accordingly, we propose and intend to pursue further investigations to test and confirm the nature of the observed high-Tc transitions, and to obtain larger high-Tc fractions by optimizing the intercalation materials and synthesis methods.
item.dc:creator: Vadim Ksenofontov, Vasily S. Minkov, Alexander P. Drozdov, Ulrich P\"oschl, Mikhail I. Eremets

item.title: Is the Kaniadakis deformation of holographic dark energy detectable? A non-flat analysis with DESI DR2, cosmic chronometers and Pantheon+SH0ES
item.description: arXiv:2610.26883v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Kaniadakis entropy deforms the horizon entropy through one parameter $\kappa$, and holographic dark energy built on it (KHDE) reduces to standard holographic dark energy (HDE) when $\kappa\to0$. The deformation enters the equations through the dimensionless combination $\beta=KM_p^2/H_0^2$, where $K$ is the effective KHDE parameter. We test whether current data detect it in a curved universe without CMB information. We combine Pantheon+SH0ES supernovae calibrated with Cepheids, 32 cosmic-chronometer measurements of $H(z)$ with their correlated systematic errors, and DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations with a free sound horizon. Non-flat KHDE fits the data as well as flat $\Lambda$CDM ($\Delta\chi^2=-3.0$), but $\beta$ is not detected: the profile $\chi^2$ changes by only 0.44 between $\beta=0$ and its best value, and by 0.46 in the flat case. The upper limit $\beta<0.65$ (95%) comes from the condition that the model has a real solution, not from the data; where the truncated expansion is reliable, the limit is $\beta<0.57$. $\beta$ of order one corresponds to $\kappa$ of order $10^{-122}$. Comparing flat and non-flat HDE and KHDE with $\Lambda$CDM shows that neither curvature nor the deformation improves the fit enough to justify the extra parameters. The joint fit gives $\Omega_{k0}=0.007\pm0.046$, $H_0=72.85\pm0.94$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$ and $r_d=137.41\pm1.88$ Mpc. The expansion starts to accelerate at $z_t=0.66\pm0.03$, and a neural-network reconstruction of $H(z)$ from the chronometers agrees with the model.
item.dc:creator: P. Suresh Kumar, Said Salim AL Kathiri
